data.why: The repo ships small, versioned synthetic example files (interrogator time-series export, an OSA-style spectrum, and a gas-switching event table) made for exactly this pipeline; make_synthetic_data.py already generated them and they are tracked in git, so no files need to be authored.

goals: Load a raw FBG interrogator export and assign interrogator channels to named sensors with their wavelength bands
Clean the raw signal: mark invalid/lost peaks, repair the time base, remove nulls and outliers
Smooth and convert the signal to wavelength shift (delta-lambda) relative to a baseline
Apply reference-grating temperature compensation to isolate the strain/measurand signal from thermal drift
Mark time intervals/events on the processed signal and compute interval statistics (mean, drift, noise, steady-state)
Build a publication-quality figure (stacked or overlaid panels) from the processed CSV and export it

review.summary: The tree follows the README's main path faithfully: clean the interrogator signal, convert to Δλ and compensate with the reference grating, then mark events, compute interval statistics and build the publication figure, with the cited screens backing nearly every node. It needs small fixes before filing: drop the misuse task, fold the zoom gesture into a task, correct two specific labels, log the chart bugs the replay found, and record the multi-file and spectral-evolution workflows as gaps.
